items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: my mother decided to come back to Cincinnati and live with an aunt whose name was Mary.

ctx.x: A few white people lived in Centerville, but most of the white men seen around the general store were farmers who lived outside the village. Most of the negro men worked on the surrounding farms and some worked on the railroad which ran from Paris to Georgetown, a distance of 19 miles. Centerville is 7 miles from Paris and 17 miles from Lexington, Ky., and like many towns and cities that I was to know about, and visit in later years, Centerville had its music. My father played the snare drum in the hometown band,…

About two years later, my mother decided to come back to Cincinnati and live with an aunt whose name was Mary. Aunt Mary smoked a pipe as did sommany women from the South. Kentucky is not what is called the deep South but the problems of the Negro were the same as those that existed in any of the other Southern states. I mentioned this because I mentioned my Aunt Mary smoking a pipe, as I said before most women from the South smoked pipes,even the white ones. Aunt Mary was also a great beer drinker. There was a…

and take it, fill it up for 5 cents, give it back to me under the swinging doors and also give me a handful of pretzels. I learned to do many useful things that have been very helpful to me in later years when we lived with my Aunt Mary. A child could not be lazy at the age of 8 years around her. So I had to sweep the floors, scrub the front and back steps every Saturday because we lived on the second floor.
